912.clozeText: Ecotourism, often defined as responsible travel to fragile, pristine natural environments that conserves biodiversity and improves the well-being of local populations, has gained tremendous momentum worldwide. Unlike conventional mass tourism that frequently leaves a trail of ecological degradation, ecotourism prioritizes environmental education and active (23) ________. Travelers participating in ecotours are encouraged to minimize their carbon (24) ________, respect indigenous cultural taboos, and purchase handmade artisanal souvenirs directly from host families. In Viet Nam, national parks like Cuc Phuong and Bach Ma offer exceptional ecotourism programs where visitors hike through ancient forests and participate in wildlife rescue (25) ________. Revenue generated from entrance tariffs and guided trekking fees is reinvested into anti-poaching patrols and habitat (26) ________ without compromising planetary (27) ________.
912.readingText: The phenomenon of World Englishes acknowledges that the English language no longer belongs exclusively to traditional inner-circle nations like the United Kingdom, the United States, or Australia. Linguist Braj Kachru proposed the influential Three Concentric Circles' model to illustrate the global spread of English: the Inner Circle (native speakers), the Outer Circle (countries where English is an institutionalized second language, such as India, Singapore, and the Philippines), and the Expanding Circle (countries where English is learned as a dominant foreign language, such as Viet Nam, Japan, and Germany). As international communications accelerate via digital internet platforms, Expanding Circle speakers increasingly use English to converse with other non-native speakers rather than native speakers. Consequently, mutual intelligibility and pragmatic communication skills are considered far more crucial than mimicking an idealized native accent.
912.passageText:
📖 ĐOẠN VĂN ĐIỀN TỪ (CLOZE TEXT - PART 4):
Ecotourism, often defined as responsible travel to fragile, pristine natural environments that conserves biodiversity and improves the well-being of local populations, has gained tremendous momentum worldwide. Unlike conventional mass tourism that frequently leaves a trail of ecological degradation, ecotourism prioritizes environmental education and active (23) ________. Travelers participating in ecotours are encouraged to minimize their carbon (24) ________, respect indigenous cultural taboos, and purchase handmade artisanal souvenirs directly from host families. In Viet Nam, national parks like Cuc Phuong and Bach Ma offer exceptional ecotourism programs where visitors hike through ancient forests and participate in wildlife rescue (25) ________. Revenue generated from entrance tariffs and guided trekking fees is reinvested into anti-poaching patrols and habitat (26) ________ without compromising planetary (27) ________.

📖 ĐOẠN VĂN ĐỌC HIỂU (READING COMPREHENSION - PART 5):
The phenomenon of World Englishes acknowledges that the English language no longer belongs exclusively to traditional inner-circle nations like the United Kingdom, the United States, or Australia. Linguist Braj Kachru proposed the influential Three Concentric Circles' model to illustrate the global spread of English: the Inner Circle (native speakers), the Outer Circle (countries where English is an institutionalized second language, such as India, Singapore, and the Philippines), and the Expanding Circle (countries where English is learned as a dominant foreign language, such as Viet Nam, Japan, and Germany). As international communications accelerate via digital internet platforms, Expanding Circle speakers increasingly use English to converse with other non-native speakers rather than native speakers. Consequently, mutual intelligibility and pragmatic communication skills are considered far more crucial than mimicking an idealized native accent.
912.writingRubric: 1. Task Response / Content: 0.25 pt | 2. Coherence & Cohesion: 0.25 pt | 3. Lexical Resource: 0.25 pt | 4. Grammatical Accuracy: 0.25 pt. Total: 1.0 point.
912.sampleWritingText: English serves as an indispensable bridge in contemporary global communication and international collaboration. Firstly, as the preeminent lingua franca across science, digital technology, and international diplomacy, English enables scholars and young professionals to access limitless databases of human knowledge and exchange ideas seamlessly. Secondly, mastering English opens doors to prestigious international universities and multicultural career pathways. By becoming proficient in English while cherishing our Vietnamese identity, we can confidently introduce our vibrant national culture to the world.

913.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Nam:: Have you decided where to spend your summer vacation, Emma?
Emma:: Yes Nam! My family has booked an ecotourism expedition in Cat Tien National Park.
Nam:: What activities will you participate in during the tour?
Emma:: We will go on guided jungle treks to observe rare gibbons and night wildlife safaris with park rangers.
Nam:: How does ecotourism differ from ordinary mass tourism?
Emma:: Ecotourism minimizes environmental disturbance, educates travelers on conservation, and channels revenue directly into local community welfare.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
English has firmly established itself as the preeminent global lingua franca in diplomacy, international commerce, science, and technological innovation. Across the globe, there are now more non-native speakers of English than native speakers, giving rise to diverse World Englishes' such as Singlish, Indian English, and Euro-English. Each variety assimilates unique local vocabulary, cultural idioms, and pronunciation nuances while retaining universal grammatical coherence. Mastering English empowers young Vietnamese professionals to articulate national viewpoints on global forums, engage in international academic exchange, and access limitless repositories of human knowledge.

913.clozeText: Ecotourism, often defined as responsible travel to fragile, pristine natural environments that conserves biodiversity and improves the well-being of local populations, has gained tremendous momentum worldwide. Unlike conventional mass tourism that frequently leaves a trail of ecological degradation, ecotourism prioritizes environmental education and active (23) ________. Travelers participating in ecotours are encouraged to minimize their carbon (24) ________, respect indigenous cultural taboos, and purchase handmade artisanal souvenirs directly from host families. In Viet Nam, national parks like Cuc Phuong and Bach Ma offer exceptional ecotourism programs where visitors hike through ancient forests and participate in wildlife rescue (25) ________. Revenue generated from entrance tariffs and guided trekking fees is reinvested into anti-poaching patrols and habitat (26) ________ without compromising planetary (27) ________.
913.readingText: The phenomenon of World Englishes acknowledges that the English language no longer belongs exclusively to traditional inner-circle nations like the United Kingdom, the United States, or Australia. Linguist Braj Kachru proposed the influential Three Concentric Circles' model to illustrate the global spread of English: the Inner Circle (native speakers), the Outer Circle (countries where English is an institutionalized second language, such as India, Singapore, and the Philippines), and the Expanding Circle (countries where English is learned as a dominant foreign language, such as Viet Nam, Japan, and Germany). As international communications accelerate via digital internet platforms, Expanding Circle speakers increasingly use English to converse with other non-native speakers rather than native speakers. Consequently, mutual intelligibility and pragmatic communication skills are considered far more crucial than mimicking an idealized native accent.

914.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ GIỮA HỌC KÌ II - LỚP 9
914.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Nam:: Have you decided where to spend your summer vacation, Emma?
Emma:: Yes Nam! My family has booked an ecotourism expedition in Cat Tien National Park.
Nam:: What activities will you participate in during the tour?
Emma:: We will go on guided jungle treks to observe rare gibbons and night wildlife safaris with park rangers.
Nam:: How does ecotourism differ from ordinary mass tourism?
Emma:: Ecotourism minimizes environmental disturbance, educates travelers on conservation, and channels revenue directly into local community welfare.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
English has firmly established itself as the preeminent global lingua franca in diplomacy, international commerce, science, and technological innovation. Across the globe, there are now more non-native speakers of English than native speakers, giving rise to diverse World Englishes' such as Singlish, Indian English, and Euro-English. Each variety assimilates unique local vocabulary, cultural idioms, and pronunciation nuances while retaining universal grammatical coherence. Mastering English empowers young Vietnamese professionals to articulate national viewpoints on global forums, engage in international academic exchange, and access limitless repositories of human knowledge.

914.clozeText: Ecotourism, often defined as responsible travel to fragile, pristine natural environments that conserves biodiversity and improves the well-being of local populations, has gained tremendous momentum worldwide. Unlike conventional mass tourism that frequently leaves a trail of ecological degradation, ecotourism prioritizes environmental education and active (23) ________. Travelers participating in ecotours are encouraged to minimize their carbon (24) ________, respect indigenous cultural taboos, and purchase handmade artisanal souvenirs directly from host families. In Viet Nam, national parks like Cuc Phuong and Bach Ma offer exceptional ecotourism programs where visitors hike through ancient forests and participate in wildlife rescue (25) ________. Revenue generated from entrance tariffs and guided trekking fees is reinvested into anti-poaching patrols and habitat (26) ________ without compromising planetary (27) ________.
914.readingText: The phenomenon of World Englishes acknowledges that the English language no longer belongs exclusively to traditional inner-circle nations like the United Kingdom, the United States, or Australia. Linguist Braj Kachru proposed the influential Three Concentric Circles' model to illustrate the global spread of English: the Inner Circle (native speakers), the Outer Circle (countries where English is an institutionalized second language, such as India, Singapore, and the Philippines), and the Expanding Circle (countries where English is learned as a dominant foreign language, such as Viet Nam, Japan, and Germany). As international communications accelerate via digital internet platforms, Expanding Circle speakers increasingly use English to converse with other non-native speakers rather than native speakers. Consequently, mutual intelligibility and pragmatic communication skills are considered far more crucial than mimicking an idealized native accent.

915.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ GIỮA HỌC KÌ II - LỚP 9
915.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Nam:: Have you decided where to spend your summer vacation, Emma?
Emma:: Yes Nam! My family has booked an ecotourism expedition in Cat Tien National Park.
Nam:: What activities will you participate in during the tour?
Emma:: We will go on guided jungle treks to observe rare gibbons and night wildlife safaris with park rangers.
Nam:: How does ecotourism differ from ordinary mass tourism?
Emma:: Ecotourism minimizes environmental disturbance, educates travelers on conservation, and channels revenue directly into local community welfare.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
English has firmly established itself as the preeminent global lingua franca in diplomacy, international commerce, science, and technological innovation. Across the globe, there are now more non-native speakers of English than native speakers, giving rise to diverse World Englishes' such as Singlish, Indian English, and Euro-English. Each variety assimilates unique local vocabulary, cultural idioms, and pronunciation nuances while retaining universal grammatical coherence. Mastering English empowers young Vietnamese professionals to articulate national viewpoints on global forums, engage in international academic exchange, and access limitless repositories of human knowledge.

915.clozeText: Ecotourism, often defined as responsible travel to fragile, pristine natural environments that conserves biodiversity and improves the well-being of local populations, has gained tremendous momentum worldwide. Unlike conventional mass tourism that frequently leaves a trail of ecological degradation, ecotourism prioritizes environmental education and active (23) ________. Travelers participating in ecotours are encouraged to minimize their carbon (24) ________, respect indigenous cultural taboos, and purchase handmade artisanal souvenirs directly from host families. In Viet Nam, national parks like Cuc Phuong and Bach Ma offer exceptional ecotourism programs where visitors hike through ancient forests and participate in wildlife rescue (25) ________. Revenue generated from entrance tariffs and guided trekking fees is reinvested into anti-poaching patrols and habitat (26) ________ without compromising planetary (27) ________.
915.readingText: The phenomenon of World Englishes acknowledges that the English language no longer belongs exclusively to traditional inner-circle nations like the United Kingdom, the United States, or Australia. Linguist Braj Kachru proposed the influential Three Concentric Circles' model to illustrate the global spread of English: the Inner Circle (native speakers), the Outer Circle (countries where English is an institutionalized second language, such as India, Singapore, and the Philippines), and the Expanding Circle (countries where English is learned as a dominant foreign language, such as Viet Nam, Japan, and Germany). As international communications accelerate via digital internet platforms, Expanding Circle speakers increasingly use English to converse with other non-native speakers rather than native speakers. Consequently, mutual intelligibility and pragmatic communication skills are considered far more crucial than mimicking an idealized native accent.
915.passageText:
📖 ĐOẠN VĂN ĐIỀN TỪ (CLOZE TEXT - PART 4):
Ecotourism, often defined as responsible travel to fragile, pristine natural environments that conserves biodiversity and improves the well-being of local populations, has gained tremendous momentum worldwide. Unlike conventional mass tourism that frequently leaves a trail of ecological degradation, ecotourism prioritizes environmental education and active (23) ________. Travelers participating in ecotours are encouraged to minimize their carbon (24) ________, respect indigenous cultural taboos, and purchase handmade artisanal souvenirs directly from host families. In Viet Nam, national parks like Cuc Phuong and Bach Ma offer exceptional ecotourism programs where visitors hike through ancient forests and participate in wildlife rescue (25) ________. Revenue generated from entrance tariffs and guided trekking fees is reinvested into anti-poaching patrols and habitat (26) ________ without compromising planetary (27) ________.

📖 ĐOẠN VĂN ĐỌC HIỂU (READING COMPREHENSION - PART 5):
The phenomenon of World Englishes acknowledges that the English language no longer belongs exclusively to traditional inner-circle nations like the United Kingdom, the United States, or Australia. Linguist Braj Kachru proposed the influential Three Concentric Circles' model to illustrate the global spread of English: the Inner Circle (native speakers), the Outer Circle (countries where English is an institutionalized second language, such as India, Singapore, and the Philippines), and the Expanding Circle (countries where English is learned as a dominant foreign language, such as Viet Nam, Japan, and Germany). As international communications accelerate via digital internet platforms, Expanding Circle speakers increasingly use English to converse with other non-native speakers rather than native speakers. Consequently, mutual intelligibility and pragmatic communication skills are considered far more crucial than mimicking an idealized native accent.

915.sampleWritingText: English serves as an indispensable bridge in contemporary global communication and international collaboration. Firstly, as the preeminent lingua franca across science, digital technology, and international diplomacy, English enables scholars and young professionals to access limitless databases of human knowledge and exchange ideas seamlessly. Secondly, mastering English opens doors to prestigious international universities and multicultural career pathways. By becoming proficient in English while cherishing our Vietnamese identity, we can confidently introduce our vibrant national culture to the world.

916.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Nam:: Have you decided where to spend your summer vacation, Emma?
Emma:: Yes Nam! My family has booked an ecotourism expedition in Cat Tien National Park.
Nam:: What activities will you participate in during the tour?
Emma:: We will go on guided jungle treks to observe rare gibbons and night wildlife safaris with park rangers.
Nam:: How does ecotourism differ from ordinary mass tourism?
Emma:: Ecotourism minimizes environmental disturbance, educates travelers on conservation, and channels revenue directly into local community welfare.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
English has firmly established itself as the preeminent global lingua franca in diplomacy, international commerce, science, and technological innovation. Across the globe, there are now more non-native speakers of English than native speakers, giving rise to diverse World Englishes' such as Singlish, Indian English, and Euro-English. Each variety assimilates unique local vocabulary, cultural idioms, and pronunciation nuances while retaining universal grammatical coherence. Mastering English empowers young Vietnamese professionals to articulate national viewpoints on global forums, engage in international academic exchange, and access limitless repositories of human knowledge.

916.clozeText: Ecotourism, often defined as responsible travel to fragile, pristine natural environments that conserves biodiversity and improves the well-being of local populations, has gained tremendous momentum worldwide. Unlike conventional mass tourism that frequently leaves a trail of ecological degradation, ecotourism prioritizes environmental education and active (23) ________. Travelers participating in ecotours are encouraged to minimize their carbon (24) ________, respect indigenous cultural taboos, and purchase handmade artisanal souvenirs directly from host families. In Viet Nam, national parks like Cuc Phuong and Bach Ma offer exceptional ecotourism programs where visitors hike through ancient forests and participate in wildlife rescue (25) ________. Revenue generated from entrance tariffs and guided trekking fees is reinvested into anti-poaching patrols and habitat (26) ________ without compromising planetary (27) ________.
916.readingText: The phenomenon of World Englishes acknowledges that the English language no longer belongs exclusively to traditional inner-circle nations like the United Kingdom, the United States, or Australia. Linguist Braj Kachru proposed the influential Three Concentric Circles' model to illustrate the global spread of English: the Inner Circle (native speakers), the Outer Circle (countries where English is an institutionalized second language, such as India, Singapore, and the Philippines), and the Expanding Circle (countries where English is learned as a dominant foreign language, such as Viet Nam, Japan, and Germany). As international communications accelerate via digital internet platforms, Expanding Circle speakers increasingly use English to converse with other non-native speakers rather than native speakers. Consequently, mutual intelligibility and pragmatic communication skills are considered far more crucial than mimicking an idealized native accent.

917.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ GIỮA HỌC KÌ II - LỚP 9
917.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Nam:: Have you decided where to spend your summer vacation, Emma?
Emma:: Yes Nam! My family has booked an ecotourism expedition in Cat Tien National Park.
Nam:: What activities will you participate in during the tour?
Emma:: We will go on guided jungle treks to observe rare gibbons and night wildlife safaris with park rangers.
Nam:: How does ecotourism differ from ordinary mass tourism?
Emma:: Ecotourism minimizes environmental disturbance, educates travelers on conservation, and channels revenue directly into local community welfare.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
English has firmly established itself as the preeminent global lingua franca in diplomacy, international commerce, science, and technological innovation. Across the globe, there are now more non-native speakers of English than native speakers, giving rise to diverse World Englishes' such as Singlish, Indian English, and Euro-English. Each variety assimilates unique local vocabulary, cultural idioms, and pronunciation nuances while retaining universal grammatical coherence. Mastering English empowers young Vietnamese professionals to articulate national viewpoints on global forums, engage in international academic exchange, and access limitless repositories of human knowledge.

917.clozeText: Ecotourism, often defined as responsible travel to fragile, pristine natural environments that conserves biodiversity and improves the well-being of local populations, has gained tremendous momentum worldwide. Unlike conventional mass tourism that frequently leaves a trail of ecological degradation, ecotourism prioritizes environmental education and active (23) ________. Travelers participating in ecotours are encouraged to minimize their carbon (24) ________, respect indigenous cultural taboos, and purchase handmade artisanal souvenirs directly from host families. In Viet Nam, national parks like Cuc Phuong and Bach Ma offer exceptional ecotourism programs where visitors hike through ancient forests and participate in wildlife rescue (25) ________. Revenue generated from entrance tariffs and guided trekking fees is reinvested into anti-poaching patrols and habitat (26) ________ without compromising planetary (27) ________.
917.readingText: The phenomenon of World Englishes acknowledges that the English language no longer belongs exclusively to traditional inner-circle nations like the United Kingdom, the United States, or Australia. Linguist Braj Kachru proposed the influential Three Concentric Circles' model to illustrate the global spread of English: the Inner Circle (native speakers), the Outer Circle (countries where English is an institutionalized second language, such as India, Singapore, and the Philippines), and the Expanding Circle (countries where English is learned as a dominant foreign language, such as Viet Nam, Japan, and Germany). As international communications accelerate via digital internet platforms, Expanding Circle speakers increasingly use English to converse with other non-native speakers rather than native speakers. Consequently, mutual intelligibility and pragmatic communication skills are considered far more crucial than mimicking an idealized native accent.

918.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ GIỮA HỌC KÌ II - LỚP 9
918.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Nam:: Have you decided where to spend your summer vacation, Emma?
Emma:: Yes Nam! My family has booked an ecotourism expedition in Cat Tien National Park.
Nam:: What activities will you participate in during the tour?
Emma:: We will go on guided jungle treks to observe rare gibbons and night wildlife safaris with park rangers.
Nam:: How does ecotourism differ from ordinary mass tourism?
Emma:: Ecotourism minimizes environmental disturbance, educates travelers on conservation, and channels revenue directly into local community welfare.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
English has firmly established itself as the preeminent global lingua franca in diplomacy, international commerce, science, and technological innovation. Across the globe, there are now more non-native speakers of English than native speakers, giving rise to diverse World Englishes' such as Singlish, Indian English, and Euro-English. Each variety assimilates unique local vocabulary, cultural idioms, and pronunciation nuances while retaining universal grammatical coherence. Mastering English empowers young Vietnamese professionals to articulate national viewpoints on global forums, engage in international academic exchange, and access limitless repositories of human knowledge.

918.clozeText: Ecotourism, often defined as responsible travel to fragile, pristine natural environments that conserves biodiversity and improves the well-being of local populations, has gained tremendous momentum worldwide. Unlike conventional mass tourism that frequently leaves a trail of ecological degradation, ecotourism prioritizes environmental education and active (23) ________. Travelers participating in ecotours are encouraged to minimize their carbon (24) ________, respect indigenous cultural taboos, and purchase handmade artisanal souvenirs directly from host families. In Viet Nam, national parks like Cuc Phuong and Bach Ma offer exceptional ecotourism programs where visitors hike through ancient forests and participate in wildlife rescue (25) ________. Revenue generated from entrance tariffs and guided trekking fees is reinvested into anti-poaching patrols and habitat (26) ________ without compromising planetary (27) ________.
918.readingText: The phenomenon of World Englishes acknowledges that the English language no longer belongs exclusively to traditional inner-circle nations like the United Kingdom, the United States, or Australia. Linguist Braj Kachru proposed the influential Three Concentric Circles' model to illustrate the global spread of English: the Inner Circle (native speakers), the Outer Circle (countries where English is an institutionalized second language, such as India, Singapore, and the Philippines), and the Expanding Circle (countries where English is learned as a dominant foreign language, such as Viet Nam, Japan, and Germany). As international communications accelerate via digital internet platforms, Expanding Circle speakers increasingly use English to converse with other non-native speakers rather than native speakers. Consequently, mutual intelligibility and pragmatic communication skills are considered far more crucial than mimicking an idealized native accent.
918.passageText:
📖 ĐOẠN VĂN ĐIỀN TỪ (CLOZE TEXT - PART 4):
Ecotourism, often defined as responsible travel to fragile, pristine natural environments that conserves biodiversity and improves the well-being of local populations, has gained tremendous momentum worldwide. Unlike conventional mass tourism that frequently leaves a trail of ecological degradation, ecotourism prioritizes environmental education and active (23) ________. Travelers participating in ecotours are encouraged to minimize their carbon (24) ________, respect indigenous cultural taboos, and purchase handmade artisanal souvenirs directly from host families. In Viet Nam, national parks like Cuc Phuong and Bach Ma offer exceptional ecotourism programs where visitors hike through ancient forests and participate in wildlife rescue (25) ________. Revenue generated from entrance tariffs and guided trekking fees is reinvested into anti-poaching patrols and habitat (26) ________ without compromising planetary (27) ________.

📖 ĐOẠN VĂN ĐỌC HIỂU (READING COMPREHENSION - PART 5):
The phenomenon of World Englishes acknowledges that the English language no longer belongs exclusively to traditional inner-circle nations like the United Kingdom, the United States, or Australia. Linguist Braj Kachru proposed the influential Three Concentric Circles' model to illustrate the global spread of English: the Inner Circle (native speakers), the Outer Circle (countries where English is an institutionalized second language, such as India, Singapore, and the Philippines), and the Expanding Circle (countries where English is learned as a dominant foreign language, such as Viet Nam, Japan, and Germany). As international communications accelerate via digital internet platforms, Expanding Circle speakers increasingly use English to converse with other non-native speakers rather than native speakers. Consequently, mutual intelligibility and pragmatic communication skills are considered far more crucial than mimicking an idealized native accent.

919.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ GIỮA HỌC KÌ II - LỚP 9
919.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Nam:: Have you decided where to spend your summer vacation, Emma?
Emma:: Yes Nam! My family has booked an ecotourism expedition in Cat Tien National Park.
Nam:: What activities will you participate in during the tour?
Emma:: We will go on guided jungle treks to observe rare gibbons and night wildlife safaris with park rangers.
Nam:: How does ecotourism differ from ordinary mass tourism?
Emma:: Ecotourism minimizes environmental disturbance, educates travelers on conservation, and channels revenue directly into local community welfare.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
English has firmly established itself as the preeminent global lingua franca in diplomacy, international commerce, science, and technological innovation. Across the globe, there are now more non-native speakers of English than native speakers, giving rise to diverse World Englishes' such as Singlish, Indian English, and Euro-English. Each variety assimilates unique local vocabulary, cultural idioms, and pronunciation nuances while retaining universal grammatical coherence. Mastering English empowers young Vietnamese professionals to articulate national viewpoints on global forums, engage in international academic exchange, and access limitless repositories of human knowledge.

919.clozeText: Ecotourism, often defined as responsible travel to fragile, pristine natural environments that conserves biodiversity and improves the well-being of local populations, has gained tremendous momentum worldwide. Unlike conventional mass tourism that frequently leaves a trail of ecological degradation, ecotourism prioritizes environmental education and active (23) ________. Travelers participating in ecotours are encouraged to minimize their carbon (24) ________, respect indigenous cultural taboos, and purchase handmade artisanal souvenirs directly from host families. In Viet Nam, national parks like Cuc Phuong and Bach Ma offer exceptional ecotourism programs where visitors hike through ancient forests and participate in wildlife rescue (25) ________. Revenue generated from entrance tariffs and guided trekking fees is reinvested into anti-poaching patrols and habitat (26) ________ without compromising planetary (27) ________.
919.readingText: The phenomenon of World Englishes acknowledges that the English language no longer belongs exclusively to traditional inner-circle nations like the United Kingdom, the United States, or Australia. Linguist Braj Kachru proposed the influential Three Concentric Circles' model to illustrate the global spread of English: the Inner Circle (native speakers), the Outer Circle (countries where English is an institutionalized second language, such as India, Singapore, and the Philippines), and the Expanding Circle (countries where English is learned as a dominant foreign language, such as Viet Nam, Japan, and Germany). As international communications accelerate via digital internet platforms, Expanding Circle speakers increasingly use English to converse with other non-native speakers rather than native speakers. Consequently, mutual intelligibility and pragmatic communication skills are considered far more crucial than mimicking an idealized native accent.

920.typeTitle: ĐỀ KIỂM TRA ĐÁNH GIÁ GIỮA HỌC KÌ II - LỚP 9
920.audioScript:
=== PART 1: DIALOGUE ===
Nam:: Have you decided where to spend your summer vacation, Emma?
Emma:: Yes Nam! My family has booked an ecotourism expedition in Cat Tien National Park.
Nam:: What activities will you participate in during the tour?
Emma:: We will go on guided jungle treks to observe rare gibbons and night wildlife safaris with park rangers.
Nam:: How does ecotourism differ from ordinary mass tourism?
Emma:: Ecotourism minimizes environmental disturbance, educates travelers on conservation, and channels revenue directly into local community welfare.

=== PART 2: MONOLOGUE ===
English has firmly established itself as the preeminent global lingua franca in diplomacy, international commerce, science, and technological innovation. Across the globe, there are now more non-native speakers of English than native speakers, giving rise to diverse World Englishes' such as Singlish, Indian English, and Euro-English. Each variety assimilates unique local vocabulary, cultural idioms, and pronunciation nuances while retaining universal grammatical coherence. Mastering English empowers young Vietnamese professionals to articulate national viewpoints on global forums, engage in international academic exchange, and access limitless repositories of human knowledge.

920.clozeText: Ecotourism, often defined as responsible travel to fragile, pristine natural environments that conserves biodiversity and improves the well-being of local populations, has gained tremendous momentum worldwide. Unlike conventional mass tourism that frequently leaves a trail of ecological degradation, ecotourism prioritizes environmental education and active (23) ________. Travelers participating in ecotours are encouraged to minimize their carbon (24) ________, respect indigenous cultural taboos, and purchase handmade artisanal souvenirs directly from host families. In Viet Nam, national parks like Cuc Phuong and Bach Ma offer exceptional ecotourism programs where visitors hike through ancient forests and participate in wildlife rescue (25) ________. Revenue generated from entrance tariffs and guided trekking fees is reinvested into anti-poaching patrols and habitat (26) ________ without compromising planetary (27) ________.
920.readingText: The phenomenon of World Englishes acknowledges that the English language no longer belongs exclusively to traditional inner-circle nations like the United Kingdom, the United States, or Australia. Linguist Braj Kachru proposed the influential Three Concentric Circles' model to illustrate the global spread of English: the Inner Circle (native speakers), the Outer Circle (countries where English is an institutionalized second language, such as India, Singapore, and the Philippines), and the Expanding Circle (countries where English is learned as a dominant foreign language, such as Viet Nam, Japan, and Germany). As international communications accelerate via digital internet platforms, Expanding Circle speakers increasingly use English to converse with other non-native speakers rather than native speakers. Consequently, mutual intelligibility and pragmatic communication skills are considered far more crucial than mimicking an idealized native accent.
